The important part here is that `CompositeList` becomes the source-of-truth re: maintaining `elementsRef`/`labelsRef`.

Previously, each item populated those refs [from its callback ref](https://github.com/mui/base-ui/pull/5148/changes#diff-c56a12aa02e59ddea82b623ac22cf1a3a6a3f796466725002c662b9e68fdf070L55-L71), while `CompositeList` adjusted their length and cleared them on cleanup. That split ownership was fragile because callback refs and layout-effect cleanups can run in different phases, especially in React 18 dev/StrictMode. 

With this change, items only register/unregister their node and metadata. `CompositeList` then builds `elementsRef` and `labelsRef` from its `sortedMap` so that ordering, sparse controlled indexes, labels, cleanup, and lengths all come from the same source of truth.
As for the R18 failures, it seems like `ref` callback still needs to fill the refs synchronously as a fallback?

The `OTPField` highlighted an edge case where an item could keep its guessed index because items subscribe to map changes _after_ registering themselves, and this PR now produces the sorted map during registering (before the subscription). 

AFAIUI, this wasn't a problem before because map listeners were notified after the `mapTick` state update, from within a layout effect tied to that state change, so index correction happened later in the render/effect cycle. The old callback ref writes were covering up that correction delay.

Now that the sorted map and refs are produced during registration,`elementsRef`/`labelsRef` are ready without waiting for that state/effect cycle. That means listener notification also happens earlier, so if a child subscribes _after_ registering it wouldn't get the correction snapshot. 

Long story short, we probably want to make sure we subscribe before we register, but this fix seems more correct/robust.

🟡 **A label change now costs a full list flush instead of one array write**

`label` is now a dependency of the register effect, so any item whose `label` changes unregisters and re-registers, which dirties the list and triggers `flush()`: an O(n log n) `compareDocumentPosition` sort, an O(n) `syncRefs` rebuild including a `textContent` DOM walk per item, N listener callbacks, a parent re-render, and a MutationObserver rebuild. On master, a label change was handled inside the item ref callback with a single `labelsRef.current[index] = label` write — O(1), no sort, no render.

**Failure scenario:** a 1,000-item Menu/Select with live-updating labels (localized or data-driven text) performs a full DOM-position sort plus 1,000 `textContent` reads on every label update — visible jank on low-end devices.

**Suggestion:** keep `label`/`textRef` out of the register-effect deps and publish label changes through a cheap path (e.g. store the label in a ref read by `syncRefs`, or write `labelsRef` directly when only the label changed).

ℹ️ **Duplicate or negative controlled indexes are silently accepted**

The controlled branch never validates indexes: two items passing the same `index` collide in `elementsRef.current[metadata.index]` (last write wins, the other item becomes invisible to keyboard navigation and hover resolution), and a negative index is dropped from the array while still sorting first. The PR adds a dev error for mixed modes but nothing for this adjacent, equally likely misuse of the new API.

**Failure scenario:** a consumer maps filtered items but passes the unfiltered array index with an off-by-one — one item silently unreachable via keyboard, no warning.

**Suggestion:** in dev, warn when a registration would overwrite an existing controlled index (or when `index < 0`).

ℹ️ **`elementsRef`/`labelsRef` are now populated later in the commit than before**

On master, each item wrote itself into `elementsRef.current[index]` inside its ref callback, i.e. at ref-attach time before any layout effect ran. Now the arrays are only rebuilt in this layout effect, which runs after all item-level layout effects (and, for items mounting from a nested state update, only in the follow-up render that `setMapTick` schedules — still pre-paint). I found no in-repo consumer that reads `listRef` from an item-level layout effect on mount (floating-ui `useListNavigation` reads it above `CompositeList`, after flush), so this is a heads-up for external/floating-ui-internal consumers rather than a named breakage — but it is a real narrowing of when the arrays are trustworthy within a commit.

**Suggestion:** a short comment documenting that the refs are valid only from the `CompositeList` layout effect onward would prevent surprises.

🟡 **`syncRefs` re-reads `textContent` for every item on every flush**

Every flush walks the DOM text of all N items, where master read `textContent` only in the ref callback of items whose index/label actually changed. In a JSX-children Combobox (which passes `labelsRef`) or an open 1,000-item Select, each filter keystroke or single item add/remove now performs ~N subtree text walks (~0.1–1ms at N=1000) on top of the pre-existing sort. Mitigations already exist (`label` prop, `textRef` narrowing, lists without `labelsRef` skip this entirely), so non-blocking — but this is the line most likely to show up in a large-list profile.

**Suggestion:** cache the resolved label per node at registration and only re-read `textContent` for newly registered nodes.

ℹ️ **Item-local re-registrations cause two parent renders and two observer rebuilds**

`flush()` bumps the tick unconditionally. In a commit that does not include `CompositeList` (an item re-registering from local state), the `register` bump causes render A, whose dirty-check effect flushes and bumps again, causing render B — and the MutationObserver effect (deps `[flush, mapTick]`) is torn down and rebuilt on both, the first time from a stale `sortedMapRef`. Master did one render and one rebuild. Both extra renders bail out cheaply (stable `children` element, memoized context), so this is only a note.

**Suggestion:** skip the tick bump in `flush()` when the registration bump already scheduled this render.
